instructions: Review every checkpoint in every scenario in order. Treat each checkpoint as a rendered user-visible state, not as a representative sample. For each action, compare the before and after screenshot and accessibility tree with the declared action, phase, expected identifiers, expected labels, and invariant names. Setup failures are blocked evidence and must not be reported as product defects. Assertion failures are product evidence and a declared checkpoint outcome of fail makes the acceptance run fail. Missing contracts, incomplete artifacts, or incomplete applicable live element-state capture are unverified or blocked and cannot be called a pass. A pre-launch before-frame may mark state capture not applicable because the app is not running; app-not-running evidence after an interaction is still a product or environment symptom that must be judged, not an instrumentation failure. Inspect functionality, visual hierarchy, layout, copy, affordances, accessibility, touch targets, persistence signals, performance symptoms, transitions, loading and error states, and anything a human user would find confusing or suspicious. Use automated tree-lint findings as evidence only when the evidence audit says live element-state capture is complete: trust touch-target findings for existing, enabled, and hittable controls; use the breadcrumb, frame, and tree line to locate anonymous controls; and treat symbol/repeated-row duplicate suppression as intentional lint policy. If applicable state capture is incomplete, report the run as blocked rather than inferring accessibility cleanliness from fallback lint. Then apply human judgment to the remaining visual and experience questions. Report only observable issues, name the first divergent checkpoint, distinguish confirmed failures from suspects and environmental blockers, and return one JSON object matching responseSchema.

findings.category: functionality | visual | accessibility | copy | interaction | persistence | performance | privacy | watch-sync | reliability
